chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from al-ʿAbbās, from Abī Hammām, from al-Riḍā عليه السلام, he said:
He performs tayammum for every salat (prayer) until water is found.

key_terms.الْمَاءُ: water, the basis for wudu (ablution) or ghusl (ritual bath)
key_terms.حَتَّى: until, marking the limit of the ruling
key_terms.لِكُلِّ: for every, indicating repetition for each instance
key_terms.يَتَيَمَّمُ: he performs tayammum, the dry ablution used when water is unavailable

ai.seo_question: Must a person renew tayammum for every salat (prayer) until water is found?
ai.summary: This hadith states that a person should perform tayammum for each salat (prayer) so long as water is not available. It addresses a legal ruling related to ritual purity and worship in the absence of water.
